issues.legal_issue: A registered attested document other than a will cannot be admitted without proof by an attesting witness when its execution is specifically denied.
material_facts: The dispute concerned a gift deed treated as a registered document and required by law to be attested.
The pleadings alleged that the deed was brought into existence fraudulently, that the alleged executant was bedridden and unable to execute it, and that his signature had been forged.
The High Court inferred from witness testimony that execution had not been specifically denied, without adequately considering the pleadings.
Neither attesting witness was produced to prove execution of the deed.
The appeal challenged the High Court’s application of the exception to the requirement for attesting-witness proof.
issues.conclusion: The pleadings clearly and specifically denied execution, so the exception did not apply. Because no attesting witness was produced, execution of the deed was not proved; the deed failed and conferred no right over the property it covered.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, a document required by law to be attested cannot be used in evidence unless at least one available and capable attesting witness is called to prove execution. The proviso removes that requirement for a registered document other than a will only when execution is not specifically denied. Whether there is a specific denial must be decided clearly and specifically, with consideration of the pleadings; it cannot rest on a vague or negative inference from testimony alone. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_document_admissibility and document_requires_attestation and registered_nonwill_document and execution_specifically_denied_in_pleadings and no_attesting_witness_examined

predicates.appeal_challenges_document_admissibility: A party appealed a decision admitting or relying on a disputed document.
predicates.document_requires_attestation: The disputed document was of a kind that the law required to be attested.
predicates.registered_nonwill_document: The disputed document was registered and was not a will.
predicates.execution_specifically_denied_in_pleadin: A party’s pleadings specifically denied that the person named as executant had executed the document.
predicates.no_attesting_witness_examined: The party relying on the document did not call an attesting witness to prove its execution.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a document’s admissibility and the document is required to be attested, registered, and not a will, a specific denial of execution in the pleadings together with the absence of an examined attesting witness means the document’s execution is unproved and it confers no right.
